title: Modal verbs 6: would (past habits)
note: RESCOPED 2026-09-02 from the parked duplicate of a2_used_to. WOULD for repeated past actions: We would go to the lake every summer. USED TO stays whole at a2_used_to - do not re-teach it. The one rule that matters: would does NOT work with states (*I would have a dog), only used to does. Items therefore contrast the two rather than drilling would alone. First draft 2026-09-02, rough - thicken after smoke.

cards.title: Modal verbs 6: would (past habits)
points: **would** here is not a wish. It means: this happened many times, and it stopped.

rows: something you did again and again

examples.en: We **would** go to the lake every summer.
examples.cz: Každé léto jsme jezdili k jezeru.

cards.title: Actions yes, states no
points: A **state** is not something you did — it is something that was true.

cards.title: It needs a time frame
points: Start with **when I** was… or **every…** so the habit reading is clear.

rows: When I was a child, I **would** walk to school.
*when I was a child* sets it
on its own this sounds like a wish, not a habit

cards.title: Common mistakes
points: **would** takes a plain verb, and never a state verb.

items.en: We would go to the lake every summer.
items.cz: Každé léto jsme jezdili k jezeru.
items.gap: Every summer we ____ to the lake. (go)
accepts: We would go to the lake every summer.
items.wrong: We would to go to the lake every summer.
items.explanation: **would** + the plain verb **go**. *Every summer* makes it a repeated habit.
items.explanation_cz: **would** + základní tvar **go**. *Every summer* z toho dělá opakovaný zvyk.

items.en: My grandfather would tell us stories.
accepts: My grandfather would tell us stories.
items.explanation: **tell** is an action he repeated, so **would** tell works.
items.explanation_cz: **tell** je činnost, kterou opakoval, takže **would** tell funguje.

items.en: I used to have a dog.
accepts: I used to have a dog.
items.explanation: **have** is a state here, so only **used to** works — not would.
items.explanation_cz: **have** je tady stav, takže funguje jen **used to** — ne would.

items.en: She used to be a teacher.
accepts: She used to be a teacher.
items.explanation: **be** is a state. States take **used to**, never would.
items.explanation_cz: **be** je stav. Stavy mají **used to**, nikdy would.

items.en: When I was a child, I would walk to school.
items.cz: Když jsem byl malý, chodil jsem do školy pěšky.
items.gap: When I was a child, I ____ to school. (walk)
accepts: When I was a child, I would walk to school.
items.explanation: *When I was a child* sets the frame, so **would** walk reads as a habit.
items.explanation_cz: *When I was a child* dává rámec, takže **would** walk zní jako zvyk.

items.en: We would visit my aunt at Christmas.
items.cz: O Vánocích jsme jezdili za tetou.
accepts: We would visit my aunt at Christmas.
items.explanation: **visit** is a repeated action, so **would** visit is fine.
items.explanation_cz: **visit** je opakovaná činnost, takže **would** visit je v pořádku.

items.en: I used to know him quite well.
items.cz: Dřív jsem ho znal docela dobře.
accepts: I used to know him quite well.
items.wrong: I would know him quite well.

items.en: My father would read to us every night.
items.gap: My father ____ to us every night. (read)
accepts: My father would read to us every night.
items.explanation: *Every night* plus the action **read** gives you **would** read.

items.en: They used to live in Ostrava.
accepts: They used to live in Ostrava.
items.explanation: **live** describes a state of affairs, so **used to** is the safe one here.
items.explanation_cz: **live** popisuje stav, takže **used to** je tu ta bezpečná volba.

items.en: Every winter we would build a snowman.
accepts: Every winter we would build a snowman.
items.explanation: *Every winter* sets the repeat, **build** is an action: **would** build.
items.explanation_cz: *Every winter* dává opakování, **build** je činnost: **would** build.

items.en: I used to like coffee, but now I don't.
items.cz: Dřív mi chutnala káva, ale teď ne.
items.gap: I ____ coffee, but now I don't. (like)
accepts: I used to like coffee, but now I don't.
items.wrong: I would like coffee, but now I don't.
items.explanation: **like** is a state. Note that *I would like* means something else entirely.
items.explanation_cz: **like** je stav. Pozor: *I would like* znamená něco úplně jiného.
